Lessons.Title: Compounding Interest
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: explain compounding as interest calculated on previous interest as well as principal, compare interest models over equal elapsed intervals, and interpret exponential growth in another repeated scale context. Original Edulytiks adaptation of Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition Unit 5 Lesson 16, https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/5/16/preparation.html and student lesson https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/5/16/index.html (CC BY 4.0). The publisher includes image size and compound-interest comparisons; all here are independent hypothetical numbers and not advice.

Hypothetical initial balance $1,000. Model S(t)=1000(1+0.12t) for simple interest at nominal12% per year, versus monthly-compounded C(m)=1000(1.01)^m when nominal12% annual is applied as1% each month, no taxes/fees/deposits. At 12 months, C(12)≈$1,126.83 while simple S(1)=$1,120.00. Interest-on-interest difference is approximately $6.83 after rounding currency once at the end.

An original square image with side length10cm enlarged by10% in each of two successive stages has final side10×1.1²=12.1cm, not12cm. Area changes from100cm² to(12.1)²=146.41cm², demonstrating that a linear dimension and its square differ. These examples illustrate repeated change without implying that prices, investments or images behave the same physically.

Student activity: create monthly balance table for months0,1,2,12, contrast with simple interest, explain which percentage base changes, and analyze the side-versus-area effect of two zooms. Teacher-scored rubric0–2 each for expressions, correct numerical/rounding checks, interpretation of simple versus compound, and coherent representation of the image scaling.

KeyConcepts.Title: Compound interest
KeyConcepts.Definition: Interest is applied to principal plus accumulated prior interest.
KeyConcepts.Rule: C(m)=P(1+i)^m for fixed periodic rate i.

KeyConcepts.Title: Simple interest
KeyConcepts.Definition: A fixed percentage of original principal is added per period.
KeyConcepts.Rule: S(t)=P(1+rt) under simple annual rate r.

KeyConcepts.Title: Repeated scaling and area
KeyConcepts.Definition: Repeated scaling multiplies a length by each stage factor, and its area scales by factor squared.

WorkedExamples.Title: Compare interest at one year
WorkedExamples.Question: Use simple12% and monthly compound1% on $1000.

Steps: This differs from a 21% increase in side length.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treating monthly compounding as twelve additions of $10 only
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Interest base grows after each month.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Rounding monthly balances aggressively for exact comparison
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Intermediate rounding can change a long-period value.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Calculate with sufficient precision and round final cents.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Assuming a 21% side increase means21% area increase
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Area scales with the square of length.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Compute new area from new side length.

SummaryPoints: Compounding applies each periodic multiplier to the updated balance.
Simple interest uses the initial principal each period.
Monthly1% compounded for12 months on $1000 yields about$1126.83.
Teacher reviews numerical modelling, scale reasoning and limits.
